<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B></B><B><I>Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</I></B><B> </B></FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Overview </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ARRIS,
headquartered in Suwanee, Georgia,&nbsp;is a global leader in entertainment, communications, and networking technology. Our innovations combine hardware, software, and services to enable advanced video experiences and constant connectivity across a
variety of environments&#151;for service providers, commercial verticals, small enterprises, and the hundreds of millions of people they serve. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We operate in three business segments: Customer Premises Equipment, Network&nbsp;&amp; Cloud and Enterprise Networks.&nbsp;We enable service providers, including cable, telecom, digital broadcast
satellite operators and media programmers, to deliver media, voice, and IP data services to their subscribers. We are a leader in <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">set-tops,</FONT> digital video and Internet Protocol Television distribution systems,
broadband access infrastructure platforms, and broadband data and voice CPE, which we also sell directly to consumers through retail channels.&nbsp;Our solutions are complemented by a broad array of services, including technical support, repair and
refurbishment, and system design and integration. The Enterprise Networks segment focuses on enabling constant, wireless and wired connectivity across complex and varied networking environments. It offers dedicated engineering, sales
</FONT></P>

customers and, as a result, we expect only low to modest growth in the overall capital expenditure in the markets we serve in 2018. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At the same time, supplier consolidation provides benefits of reduced costs through innovation, efficiency of working with fewer suppliers and higher

STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Capital Expenditures of Telecom Customers Have Been and May Continue to be Lower </I></B>&#151; Many of our telecom customers, including AT&amp;T and Verizon, have participated in FCC sponsored
spectrum auctions in the interest of expanding their network capacity to meet increasing customer demand. As a result, capital expenditures at our existing and potential telecom customers are expected to be lower as a result of the costs associated
with participating in the auction. The purchase of DirecTV by AT&amp;T has altered the historic AT&amp;T product strategy for video deployments, decreasing our sales. Verizon completed the sale of certain properties to Frontier, which, coupled with
a decrease in net subscriber additions, has impacted the demand for our products. Nevertheless, as described below, we still believe that the need for network expansion to meet subscriber demand presents potential opportunities for increased sales
of our products to these customers. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>The markets for both Service Provider and Enterprise
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi</FONT> are growing but are also highly competitive </I></B>&#151;<B><I> </I></B>We believe the markets for our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi</FONT> solutions are growing rapidly and our intention is to
continue to invest for long-term growth to maintain our competitiveness. We expect to continue to invest heavily in research and development to expand the capabilities of our solutions with respect to services providers and enterprises. We will
invest in migrating to cloud-based managed <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi</FONT> services as a way for organizations to further leverage investments in <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi</FONT> infrastructure. Managed <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi</FONT> services, such as the ability to use <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi</FONT> to gather detailed user analytics, demographics and user location information, allow companies to better understand network
traffic and user interactions. We also plan to continue to make significant investments in our field sales and marketing activities, both by increasing our service provider focused direct sales force and by expanding our network of channel partners.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Foreign Exchange Fluctuations Have and May Continue to Impact Demand </I></B>&#151; The majority of our international
sales are denominated in U.S. dollars. During periods where the U.S. dollar strengthens, it may impact these customers&#146; ability to purchase products, which could have a material impact on our sales in the
</FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">48 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">
affected countries. These customers may delay or reduce future purchases from us, and we may experience pricing pressures in order to maintain or increase our market share with these
international customers, and we may face longer payment cycles. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Growth of Connected Device Ecosystem</I></B> &#151;
Consumers&#146; growing appetite for connected devices creates an unprecedented opportunity to deliver consistent and engaging services over the Internet of Things. Service providers have an incumbent advantage in offering new forms of entertainment
and communications, but still face many challenges in delivering new services across this complex system of devices. ARRIS is in position to drive this opportunity for providers as a result of our expertise in full-cycle service delivery &#151; from
the network to the cloud and the home. We provide the portfolio and professional services to navigate this new combination of device interfaces, communications protocols, device management standards, and security considerations. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Wireline Broadband Service Providers may Evolve into partial or predominantly Wireless Network Operators </I></B>&#151; As consumer
and business demand for ubiquitous connectivity for their devices continues to increase, wireline operators may shift or increase investment into wireless technologies such as <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi,</FONT> LTE Small Cell, or the
emerging Citizen&#146;s Band Radio Service (&#147;CBRS&#148;).&nbsp;ARRIS is positioned to participate in Service Provider&#146;s residential wireless investments with our portfolio of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi</FONT> enabled cable
modems and DSL modems. With the recently completed Ruckus Networks acquisition, we now also have a portfolio of Access Points, Controllers, Cloud Management, and Data Analytics to participate in opportunities in both the enterprise market and
Service Provider public access (e.g. hot spots). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Network Optimization and Scaling Infrastructure to Keep Up with
Increasing Consumer Bandwidth Demand</I></B> &#151; As service providers prepare to deliver more advanced services to subscribers &#151; such as 4K TV, IoT, gigabit <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Wi-Fi</FONT> &#151; they are investing increasingly
in their networks to anticipate the reciprocal need for more bandwidth. Providers are looking to ARRIS for its leadership in technologies like DOCSIS, CCAP, and DAA to scale to these multi-gigabit services and ARRIS continues to invest in R&amp;D to
keep its customers&#146; networks ahead of market demand for these services. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Competition Increasing between Cable
Operators, Telecom Companies, and New Entrants </I></B><I>&#151;</I> The lines between telecom and cable providers has blurred as each has embraced the triple play. Moreover, OTT market participants and individual programming networks have entered
the market with competing products placing higher bandwidth demands on the network. This competition emphasizes the enabling technologies behind each approach &#151; including DOCSIS, fiber, G.Fast, and others &#151; and the increasing investment in
the network infrastructure and CPE required to deliver these services. ARRIS&#146;s leadership across these solutions positions us to capitalize on the growing competition between all three stakeholders. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Service Providers are Demanding Advanced Network Technologies and Software Solutions </I></B><I>&#151;</I><B><I> </I></B>The
increase in volume and complexity of the signals transmitted over broadband networks as a result of the migration to an <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">all-digital,</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">all-IP,</FONT> on demand network is causing
service providers to deploy new technologies. Service providers also are demanding sophisticated network and service management software applications that minimize operating expenditures needed to support the complexity of <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">two-way</FONT> broadband communications systems. As a result, service providers are focusing on technologies and products that are flexible, cost-effective, compliant with open industry standards, and scalable to meet
subscriber growth and effectively deliver reliable, enhanced services. As part of this evolution, some operators (for example Comcast with its Reference Design Kit (&#147;RDK&#148;) efforts) are choosing to design portions of the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">set-tops</FONT> firmware internally. As a result, we anticipate that over time operators will migrate to an all IP network and look to enable new platforms and technologies intended to accelerate the deployment of new
services. As this occurs, which we believe will be over a multi-year period, we anticipate a decline in demand for our traditional <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">set-tops</FONT> and an increase in demand in new IP
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">set-tops.</FONT> </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Results of Operations </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Overview </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As highlighted above, we have faced, and in the future, will face significant changes in our industry and business. These changes have impacted our results of operations and are expected to do so in the
future. As a result, we have implemented strategies both in anticipation and in reaction to the impact of these dynamics. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>Customer Premises Equipment Net Sales 2017 vs. 2016 </U></I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, sales in our CPE segment decreased by approximately $271.8&nbsp;million, or 5.7%, as
compared to 2016. Video CPE sales declined due to lower volumes and were partially offset by increased Broadband CPE sales due to growth in our DOCSIS portfolio as compared to the same period in 2016. We anticipate the continued trend towards more
broadband CPE sales and less video CPE sales as operators adopt all IP networks. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>Network&nbsp;&amp; Cloud Net Sales
2017 vs. 2016 </U></I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, sales in the N&amp;C segment decreased by approximately
$17.6&nbsp;million, or 0.8%, as compared to 2016. The decrease in sales was primarily a result of lower CMTS hardware sales, which were impacted by the timing of the introduction of our next generation products, as well as lower video product sales.
This decrease was partially offset by higher Access Technologies products and software and services sales, as operators continue to build out their networks to accommodate higher bandwidth needs. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>Enterprise Networks Net Sales 2017 vs. 2016 </U> </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, sales in the Enterprise segment was approximately $45.7&nbsp;million, primarily a result of the acquisition of Ruckus Networks. Sales in the Enterprise
Networks include revenues from sales to service providers that were previously included in the Network and Cloud segment when we were a reseller of Ruckus products. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>Customer Premises Equipment Net Sales 2016 vs. 2015 </U> </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2016, sales in our CPE segment increased by approximately $1,610.9&nbsp;million, or 51.3%, as compared to 2015. The increase was primarily attributable to expansion of both video and broadband products resulting from the
Pace combination and our customers&#146; ongoing investment in CPE technology to improve the offering to their subscribers. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>Network</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;&amp; Cloud Net Sales 2016 vs. 2015 </U> </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2016, sales in the N&amp;C segment increased by approximately $450.1&nbsp;million, or 27.1%, as
compared to 2015. The increase in sales was primarily a result of the Pace combination and increased customer spend as service providers increase their investment to expand broadband network capacity and high-speed data Internet access speeds.

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, gross margin dollars decreased as compared to the same
period in 2016 primarily due to lower sales, a change in product and customer mix, timing of product introductions and memory pricing increases. Pressures on gross margin relating to memory pricing and the competitive landscape for some of our
products, particularly in the CPE segment, are expected to continue in the near term and could make it difficult to return to historical gross margin levels. In addition, the gross margins were impacted by $8.5&nbsp;million in 2017 associated with
writing up the historic cost of inventory, related to acquired businesses, to fair value at the date of acquisition thereby increasing cost of goods sold. The Ruckus Networks acquisition also impacted the gross margin for 2017, due to a
proportionately higher average gross margin than the historic ARRIS business. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2016,
gross margin dollars increased primarily due to the Pace combination as compared to 2015. The gross margin percentage decreased primarily due to product mix as compared to 2015. We had a change in mix within our CPE segment, reflecting higher sales
of lower margin products. We also had higher sales of CPE products compared to Network and Cloud products. CPE sales have a lower margin than the consolidated average. The gross margin for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2016 included a
$51.4&nbsp;million impact associated with writing up the historic cost of the Pace inventory to fair value at the date of acquisition. In addition, the gross margins were impacted by $30.2&nbsp;million associated with a reduction in sales associated
with the fair value of the warrant issued to customers. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Operating Expenses </I></FONT></P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2017, we have embarked on significant enhancements to our business processes and Enterprise Resource
Planning (&#147;ERP&#148;) systems.&nbsp;During 2017, we incurred $ 12.7&nbsp;million related to this global ERP effort which is projected to continue into 2019. We expect this project to incur approximately $5.0&nbsp;million per quarter going
forward. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">52 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Selling, General, and Administrative, or SG&amp;A, Expenses </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our selling, general and administrative expenses include sales and marketing costs, including personnel expenses for sales and marketing
staff expenses, advertising, trade shows, corporate communications, product marketing expenses and other marketing expenses. In addition, general and administrative expenses consist of personnel expenses and other general corporate expenses for
corporate executives, finance and accounting, human resources, facilities, information technology, legal and professional fees. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>2017 vs. 2016 </U></I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The year-over-year increase in SG&amp;A expenses reflects the inclusion of expenses associated with the Ruckus Networks acquisition. In addition, we incurred higher legal fees and professional services,
which were partially offset by lower expenses due to reductions in force following the Pace combination in 2016. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>2016
vs. 2015 </U></I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The year-over-year increase in SG&amp;A expenses primarily reflected the inclusion of incremental expenses
associated with the Pace combination, as well as higher variable compensation costs. Costs were reduced through the year as Pace was integrated into ARRIS. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Research&nbsp;&amp; Development, or R&amp;D, Expenses </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Research and
development expenses consist primarily of personnel expenses, payments to suppliers for design services, product certification expenditures to qualify our products for sale into specific markets, prototypes, other consulting fees and reasonable
allocations of our information technology and corporate facility costs. Research and development expenses are recognized as they are incurred. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>2017 vs. 2016 </U></I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The decrease year-over-year in R&amp;D expense
reflected the result of reduction in force following the Pace combination and the divestiture of certain product lines that occurred during 2016. The decrease was partially offset by an increase from the inclusion of expenses associated with the
Ruckus Networks acquisition. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>2016 vs. 2015 </U></I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The increase year-over-year in R&amp;D expense reflected the inclusion of incremental expenses associated with the expanded product
portfolio with our acquisition of Pace. Costs were reduced through the year as Pace was integrated into ARRIS. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Amortization of Intangible Assets </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our intangible amortization expense relates to finite-lived intangible assets primarily acquired in business combinations. Intangibles amortization expense was $375.4&nbsp;million in 2017, as compared
with $397.5 and $227.4&nbsp;million in 2016 and 2015, respectively. The decrease in amortization expense resulted from certain intangible assets becoming fully amortized, which was partially offset by an increase in amortization expense from
acquired intangibles associated with the Ruckus acquisition. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Impairment of Goodwill and Intangible Assets </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the fourth quarter of 2017, we recorded partial impairments of goodwill and indefinite-lived tradenames of $51.2&nbsp;million and
$3.8&nbsp;million, respectively, acquired in our ActiveVideo acquisition and included as part of our Cloud TV reporting unit, of which $19.3&nbsp;million is attributable to the noncontrolling interest. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition, we will adopt new guidance on revenue recognition as of January&nbsp;1, 2018. As a result of retrospective application of
this guidance, an additional goodwill impairment of approximately $5 million to $8 million is expected to be recognized in our Cloud TV reporting unit in first quarter of 2018, resulting from the indirect effect of the change in accounting
principle, effecting changes in the composition and carrying amount of the net assets. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">53 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2016, we <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">wrote-off</FONT> $2.2&nbsp;million related
to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-process</FONT> research and development projects acquired in the Pace combination that were subsequently abandoned. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Integration, Acquisition, Restructuring and Other Costs </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2017, we
recorded acquisition related expenses and integration expenses of $77.4&nbsp;million. These expenses are primarily due to the acquisition of Ruckus Networks and include $61.5&nbsp;million related to the cash settlement of stock-based awards held by
transferring employees, as well as banker and other fees. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2016, we recorded acquisition related expenses and
integration expenses of $53.2&nbsp;million. These expenses related to the Pace combination and consisted of banker fees, legal fees, integration related outside services and other direct costs of the combination. The Company substantially completed
its integration of the Pace business in 2016. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2015, we recorded acquisition related expenses and integration expenses
of $28.2&nbsp;million. The expenses in 2015 were primarily related to the Pace combination completed in 2016 and the ActiveVideo acquisition. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2017, 2016 and 2015, we recorded restructuring charges of $20.9&nbsp;million, $96.3&nbsp;million and $1.0&nbsp;million, respectively. The charge in 2017 primarily related to employee severance and
contractual obligation costs. The restructuring plan affected approximately 195 positions across the Company and its reportable segments. The charges in 2016 primarily related to employee severance and contractual obligation costs. The restructuring
plan affected approximately 1,545 positions across the Company and its reportable segments. The charges in 2015 were related to severance and employee termination benefits. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Other costs of $8.6&nbsp;million was recorded during 2016 of which $1.1&nbsp;million was related to the loss resulting from the divestitures of certain product lines and $7.5&nbsp;million was related to
the loss on disposal of property, plant and equipment. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Direct Contribution </I></B></FONT></P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Customer Premises Equipment Direct Contribution 2017 vs. 2016 </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2017, direct contribution in our CPE segment decreased by approximately 27.3% as compared to the same period in 2016. The decline
in direct contribution resulted from lower sales and product mix, as well as lower gross margin due primarily to memory pricing increases and price competition, which are expected to continue in the near-term. Year over year, memory component
pricing increased by approximately $100&nbsp;million. Our CPE reporting unit has approximately $1.4&nbsp;billion of goodwill as of December&nbsp;31, 2017.&nbsp;The estimated fair value of our CPE reporting unit is closely aligned with the ultimate
amount of revenue and operating income that it achieves, and as such, a prolonged or continued erosion in the direct contribution in the CPE segment could result in an impairment of goodwill associated with this business. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">54 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Network&nbsp;&amp; Cloud Direct Contribution 2017 vs. 2016 </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2017, direct contribution in our N&amp;C segment increased by approximately 18.3% as compared to the same period in 2016. The
increase was primarily attributable to the mix of product, including the sale of more software licenses and reductions in operating expenses. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Enterprise Networks Direct Contribution 2017 vs. 2016 </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2017, direct
contribution in our Enterprise was approximately $6.1&nbsp;million. This was primarily a result of the acquisition of Ruckus Networks. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Customer Premises Equipment Direct Contribution 2016 vs. 2015 </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2016,
direct contribution in our CPE segment increased by approximately 24.8% as compared to the same period in 2015. The increase was primarily attributable the higher sales resulting from the Pace combination, offset by higher R&amp;D, also a result of
the Pace combination. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Network&nbsp;&amp; Cloud Direct Contribution 2016 vs. 2015 </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2016, direct contribution in our N&amp;C segment increased by approximately 39.9% as compared to the same period in 2015. The
increase was primarily attributable to higher sales resulting from the Pace combination. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Corporate and Unallocated Costs
</I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">There are expenses that are not included in the measure of segment direct contribution and as such are reported as
&#147;Corporate and Unallocated Costs&#148; and are included in the reconciliation to income (loss) before income taxes. The &#147;Corporate and Unallocated Costs&#148; category of expenses include corporate sales and marketing, home office general
and administrative expenses, annual bonus and equity compensation. &#147;Corporate and Unallocated Costs&#148; also includes corporate sales and marketing for the CPE and N&amp;C segments. Marketing and Sales expenses related to the Enterprise
segment are considered a direct operating expense for that segment and are not included in the &#147;Corporate and Unallocated Costs.&#148; </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT

obligations. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Interest expense was $87.1&nbsp;million in 2017, as compared with $79.8&nbsp;million and $70.9&nbsp;million in

term loan facilities, which were included as interest expense in the Consolidated Statements of Income for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT

Consolidated Statements of Income for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Loss on Investments </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We hold certain investments in equity securities of private and publicly-traded companies and investments in rabbi trusts associated with
our deferred compensation plans, and certain investments in limited liability companies and partnerships that are accounted for using the equity method of accounting. Our equity portion in current earnings of such investments is included in the loss
(gain) on investments. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, we recorded net losses on investment
related to these investments of $11.1&nbsp;million, $21.2&nbsp;million and $6.2&nbsp;million, respectively, including impairment charges. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company performed an evaluation of its investments and concluded that indicators of impairment existed for certain investments, and that their fair value had declined. This resulted in
other-than-temporary impairment charges of $2.8&nbsp;million, $12.3&nbsp;million and $0.2&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively. </FONT></P>

federal and state taxes and other foreign taxes, which was (211.9)% of our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-tax</FONT> income of $21.2&nbsp;million. The Company&#146;s effective income tax rate for 2017 was favorably impacted by
$22.3&nbsp;million of tax rate changes primarily driven by US Tax Reform, $25.4&nbsp;million related to the generation of research and development credits primarily in the U.S., and $36.2&nbsp;million of tax benefits from other foreign tax regimes,
primarily Luxembourg and Hong Kong. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On December&nbsp;22, 2017, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (the &#147;Act&#148;) was
signed into law making significant changes to the Internal Revenue Code. Changes include, but are not limited to, a corporate tax rate decrease from 35% to 21% effective for tax years beginning after December&nbsp;31, 2017, a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> transition tax on the mandatory deemed repatriation of cumulative foreign earnings as of December&nbsp;31, 2017, a new alternative U.S. tax on certain Base Erosion Anti-Avoidance (BEAT) payments from a U.S.
company to any foreign related party, a new U.S. tax on certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">off-shore</FONT> earnings referred to as Global Intangible <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Low-Taxed</FONT> Income (GILTI), additional limitations on
certain executive compensation and limitations on interest deductions. We have calculated our best estimate of the impact of the Act in the year end income tax provision in accordance with our understanding of the Act and guidance available as of
the date of this filing and as a result has recorded ($22.5) </FONT></P>

$107.1&nbsp;million. The Company&#146;s effective income tax rate for 2015 was favorably impacted by $2.4&nbsp;million for the following items. The tax benefit was due to the release of $27.3&nbsp;million of valuation allowances primarily recorded

operating decisions. These <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures are among the factors management uses in planning for and forecasting future periods. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures should be

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures reflect adjustments based on the
following items, as well as the related income tax effects: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Reduction in Revenue Related to
Warrants</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We entered into agreements with two customers for the issuance of warrants to purchase up to 14.0&nbsp;million of ARRIS&#146;s ordinary shares. Vesting of the warrants is subject to certain purchase volume
commitments, and therefore the accounting guidance requires that we record any change in the fair value of warrants as a reduction in revenue. Until final vesting, changes in the fair value of the warrants will be marked to market and any adjustment
recorded in revenue.&nbsp;We have excluded the effect of the implied fair value in calculating our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures. We believe it is useful to understand the effects of these items on our total
revenues and gross margin. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Acquisition Accounting Impacts Related to Deferred Revenue</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
connection with the accounting related to our acquisitions, business combination rules require us to account for the fair values of deferred revenue arrangements for post contract support in our purchase accounting. The <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> adjustment to our sales and cost of sales is intended to include the full amounts of such revenues as if these purchase accounting adjustments had not been applied. We believe the adjustment to these
revenues is useful as a measure of the ongoing performance of our business. We historically have experienced high renewal rates related to our support agreements, and our objective is to increase the renewal rates on acquired post contract support
agreements. However, we cannot be certain that our customers will renew their contracts. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Stock-Based Compensation
Expense</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have excluded the effect of stock-based compensation expenses in calculating our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> operating expenses and net income (loss) measures. Although stock-based
compensation is a key incentive offered to our employees, we continue to evaluate our business performance excluding stock-based compensation expenses. We record <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</FONT> compensation expense related to grants
of restricted stock units. Depending upon the size, timing and the terms of the grants, the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</FONT> compensation expense may vary significantly but will recur in future periods. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Acquisition Accounting Impacts Related to Inventory Valuation:</U>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the accounting related to
our acquisitions, business combinations rules require the acquired inventory be recorded at fair value on the opening balance sheet.&nbsp;This is different from historical cost.&nbsp;Essentially, we are required to write the inventory up to the end
customer price less a reasonable margin as a distributor. We have excluded the resulting adjustments in inventory and cost of goods sold as the historic and forward gross margin trends will differ as a result of the adjustments. We believe it is
useful to understand the effects of this on cost of goods sold and margin. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Integration, Acquisition, Restructuring and
Other Costs</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have excluded the effect of acquisition, integration, and other expenses and the effect of restructuring expenses in calculating our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> operating expenses and
net income measures. We incurred expenses in connection with the ActiveVideo, Motorola Home, Pace and Ruckus Networks acquisitions, which we generally would not otherwise incur in the periods presented as part of our continuing operations.
Acquisition and integration expenses consist of transaction costs, costs for transitional employees, other acquired employee related costs, and integration related outside services. Restructuring expenses consist of employee severance, abandoned
facilities, product line disposition and other exit costs. We believe it is useful to understand the effects of these items on our total operating expenses. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Impairment of Goodwill and Intangible Assets</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have excluded the effect of the estimated impairment of goodwill and intangible assets in calculating our <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> operating expenses and net income measures. Although an impairment does not directly impact the Company&#146;s current cash position, such expense represents the declining value of the technology and other
intangible assets that were acquired. We exclude these impairments when significant and they are not reflective of ongoing business and operating results. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">60 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Amortization of Intangible Assets</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have excluded the effect
of amortization of intangible assets in calculating our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> operating expenses and net income (loss) measures. Amortization of intangible assets is <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cash,</FONT> and is
inconsistent in amount and frequency and is significantly affected by the timing and size of our acquisitions. Investors should note that the use of intangible assets contributed to our revenues earned during the periods presented and will
contribute to our future period revenues as well. Amortization of intangible assets will recur in future periods. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Noncontrolling Interest share of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> Adjustments</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The joint
venture formed for the ActiveVideo acquisition is accounted for by ARRIS under the consolidation method. As a result, the consolidated Statements of Income include the revenues, expenses, and gains and losses of the noncontrolling interest. The
amount of net income (loss) related to the noncontrolling interest are reported and presented separately in the consolidated Statements of Income. We have excluded the noncontrolling share of any <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-</FONT> GAAP
adjusted measures recorded by the venture, as we believe it is useful to understand the effect of excluding this item when evaluating our ongoing performance. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Impairment (Gain) on Investments</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have excluded the effect of other-than-temporary impairments and certain gains on investments in calculating our <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures. We believe it is useful to understand the effect of this <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</FONT> item in our other expense (income). </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Debt Amendment Fees</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2017 and 2015, the Company amended its credit agreement. This debt modification
allowed us to improve the terms and conditions of the credit agreement, extend the maturities of certain loan facilities, increase the amount of the revolving credit facility, and add new term loan facility. We have excluded the effect of the
associated fees in calculating our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures. We believe it is useful to understand the effect of this item in our other expense (income). </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Credit Facility &#151; Ticking Fees</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the Pace combination, the cash portion of the
consideration was funded through debt financing commitments. A ticking fee was a fee paid to our banks to compensate for the time lag between the commitment allocation on a loan and the actual funding. We have excluded the effect of the ticking fee
in calculating our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures. We believe it is useful to understand the effect of this item in our other expense (income). </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Foreign Exchange Contract Losses Related to Pace Combination</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the second quarter of 2015, the Company
announced its intent to acquire Pace in exchange for stock and cash. We subsequently entered into foreign exchange forward contracts in order to hedge the foreign currency risk associated with the cash consideration of the Pace combination. These
foreign exchange forward contracts were not designated as hedges, and accordingly, all changes in the fair value of these instruments are recognized as a loss (gain) on foreign currency in the Consolidated Statements of Income. We believe it is
useful to understand the effect of this on our other expense (income). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Remeasurement of Deferred
Taxes</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company records foreign currency remeasurement gains and losses related to deferred tax liabilities in the United Kingdom. The foreign currency remeasurement gains and losses derived from the remeasurement of
the deferred income taxes from GBP to USD. We have excluded the impact of these gains and losses in the calculation of our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures. We believe it is useful to understand the effects of this item on
our total other expense (income). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Adjustment to Liability Related to Foreign Tax Credits</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
connection with our acquisition of Motorola Home, we obtained certain foreign tax credit benefits for which we have recorded a liability to Google resulting from certain provisions in the acquisition agreement. The expense and subsequent adjustments
related to this liability has been recorded as part of other expense (income). We have excluded the effect of the expense in the calculation of our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures.&nbsp;We believe it is useful to
understand the effects of this item on our total other expense (income). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Loss on Sale of
Building</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the first quarter of 2015, the Company sold land and a building that qualified for sale-leaseback accounting and was classified as an operating lease. A loss has been recorded on the sale. We have excluded the
effect of the loss on sale of property in calculating our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures. We believe it is useful to understand the effect of excluding this item when evaluating our ongoing performance.
</FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">61 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Foreign Withholding Tax</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the Pace
combination, ARRIS U.S. Holdings, Inc. transferred shares of its subsidiary ARRIS Financing II Sarl to ARRIS International. Under U.S. tax law, based on the best available information, we believe the transfer constituted a deemed distribution from
ARRIS U.S. Holdings Inc. to ARRIS International that is treated as a dividend for U.S. tax purposes. A deemed dividend of this type is subject to U.S. withholding tax to the extent of the current and accumulated earnings and profits (as computed for
tax purposes) (&#147;E&amp;P&#148;) of ARRIS U.S. Holdings Inc., which include the E&amp;P of the former ARRIS Group and subsidiaries through December&nbsp;31, 2016. Accordingly, ARRIS U.S. Holdings Inc. remitted U.S. withholding tax in the amount
of $55&nbsp;million based upon its estimated E&amp;P of $1.1&nbsp;billion and the U.S. dividend withholding tax rate of 5&nbsp;percent (as provided in Article 10 (Dividends) of the United Kingdom-United States Tax Treaty). We have excluded the
withholding tax in calculating our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Income Tax Expense
(Benefit)</U>:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have excluded the tax effect of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> items mentioned above. Additionally, we have excluded the effects of certain tax adjustments related to tax and legal
restructuring, state valuation allowances, research and development tax credits and provision to return differences. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Financial Liquidity
and Capital Resources </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Overview </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Accounts Receivable </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We use the number of times per year that inventory turns over (based upon sales for the most recent period, or turns) to evaluate inventory management, and days sales outstanding, or DSOs, to evaluate
accounts receivable management. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Accounts receivable at the end of 2017 decreased as compared to the end of 2016, primarily
due to the timing of purchases by customers in late 2016. DSO increased in 2017, primarily reflecting a larger international mix. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Accounts receivable increased at the end of 2016 as compared to 2015, primarily due to the inclusion of sales associated with the Pace products, which were not included in 2015, as well as payment
patterns and timing of shipments to customers. As part of the Pace combination, we acquired approximately $452.3&nbsp;million of accounts receivable. Our DSO increased year over year as a result of the timing of sales and payment patterns of
customers. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Accounts receivable at the end of 2015 increased as compared to the end of 2014, primarily due to payment patterns
of our customers and timing of shipments to customers. DSOs increased reflecting a larger international mix. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Inventory
</I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Inventory at the end of 2017 increased as compared to the end of 2016, reflecting timing of shipments to customers and
anticipated demand for certain products, inventory acquired in the Ruckus acquisition, and the impact of transitioning component inventories from outsourced assemblers to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-house</FONT> production. We anticipate a
reduction in inventory in 2018. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Inventory increased at the end of 2016 as compared to 2015, primarily due to the Pace
combination. We acquired approximately $427.6&nbsp;million of inventory upon closing of the Pace combination in January 2016. Inventory turns increased year over year reflecting timing of shipments to customers. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Inventory at the end of 2015 was similar to that of the end of 2014, however, inventory turns were lower in 2015 reflecting the timing of
customer requirements and anticipated demand for certain products. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Debt Repayments and Proceeds </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2017, we repaid $91.7&nbsp;million of our term debt. With regards to our Term Loan B facility, we repaid $29.1&nbsp;million in debt to
exiting lenders and recorded proceeds from issuance of debt of $30.3&nbsp;million. With regards to our Term Loan A and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1,</FONT> we repaid $123.2&nbsp;million in debt to exiting lenders and recorded proceeds from
issuance of debt of $145.5&nbsp;million. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2016, we repaid $79.5&nbsp;million of our term debt as well as
$240.2&nbsp;million of debt assumed and settled in conjunction with the Pace combination in January 2016. In addition, we received proceeds upon the closing of the Pace combination for our Term Loan <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1</FONT>
Facility of $800&nbsp;million. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2015, we repaid $53.5&nbsp;million of our term debt, of which $38.5&nbsp;million was term
debt under our senior secured credit facilities and $15.0&nbsp;million was term debt assumed and settled in conjunction with the ActiveVideo acquisition in April 2015. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">63 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Financing Lease Obligation </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2015, we sold our San Diego office complex consisting of land and buildings. We concurrently entered into a leaseback arrangement for
two of the buildings (Building 1 and Building 2). Building 1 did not qualify for sale leaseback accounting due to continuing involvement that will exist for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10-year</FONT> lease term. Accordingly, the carrying
amount of Building 1 will remain on the Company&#146;s balance sheet and will be depreciated over the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">ten-year</FONT> lease period with the proceeds reflected as a financing obligation. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Share Repurchases </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Upon completing the Pace combination, we conducted a court-approved process in accordance with section 641(1)(b) of the UK Companies Act 2006, pursuant to which we reduced our stated share capital and
thereby increased our distributable reserves or excess capital out of which we may legally pay dividends or repurchase shares. Distributable reserves are not linked to a U.S. GAAP reported amount. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2016, our Board of Directors approved a $300&nbsp;million share repurchase authorization replacing all prior programs. In early 2017,
the Board authorized an additional $300&nbsp;million for share repurchases. Unless terminated earlier by a Board resolution, this new plan will expire when ARRIS has used all authorized funds for repurchase. The remaining authorized amount for stock
repurchases under this plan was $225.0&nbsp;million as of December&nbsp;31, 2017. However, U.K. law also generally prohibits a company from repurchasing its own shares through &#147;off market purchases&#148; without prior approval of shareholders
because we are not traded on a recognized investment exchange in the U.K. This shareholder approval lasts for a maximum period of five years. Prior to and in connection with the Pace combination, we obtained approval to purchase our own shares. This
authority to repurchase shares terminates in January 2021, unless otherwise reapproved by our shareholders. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2017, we
repurchased 7.5&nbsp;million ordinary shares for $197.0&nbsp;million at an average stock price of $26.12. During 2016, we repurchased 7.4&nbsp;million of our ordinary shares for $178.0&nbsp;million at an average stock price of $24.09. During 2015,
we repurchased 0.9&nbsp;million shares of our stock for $25.0&nbsp;million at an average stock price of $28.70. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Summary of
Current Liquidity Position and Potential for Future Capital Raising </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We believe our current liquidity position, where we
had approximately $511.4&nbsp;million of cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments on hand as of December&nbsp;31, 2017, together with approximately $498.3&nbsp;million in availability under our Revolving Credit Facility, and the prospects for
continued generation of cash from operations, are adequate for our short- and medium-term business needs. Our cash, cash-equivalents and short-term investments as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 include approximately $364.6&nbsp;million held by all <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> subsidiaries. Of that amount, $64.3&nbsp;million was held by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> subsidiaries legally owned by ARRIS U.S. entities whose earnings we expect to reinvest
indefinitely outside of the United States. We do not expect to need the cash generated by those <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> subsidiaries to fund our U.S. operations. However, in the unforeseen event that we repatriate cash from
those <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> subsidiaries, we may be required to provide for and pay U.S. taxes on permanently repatriated funds. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We have subsidiaries in countries that maintain restrictions, such as legal reserves, with respect to the dividend amount that the subsidiaries can distribute.&nbsp;Additionally, some countries impose
restrictions or controls over how and when dividends can be paid by these subsidiaries.&nbsp;While we do not currently intend to repatriate earnings from entities in these countries, if we were to be required to distribute earnings from such
countries, the timing of the distribution and the funds available to distribute, would be adversely impacted by these restrictions. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We expect to be able to generate sufficient cash on a consolidated basis to make all of the principal and interest payments under our senior secured credit facilities. Should our available funds be
insufficient to support these initiatives or our operations, it is possible that we will raise capital through private or public, share or debt offerings. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">64 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Senior Secured Credit Facilities </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On December&nbsp;20, 2017, we entered into a Fourth Amendment (the &#147;Fourth Amendment&#148;) to our Amended and Restated Credit
Facility dated June&nbsp;18, 2015, as previously amended on December&nbsp;14, 2015, April&nbsp;26, 2017, and October&nbsp;17, 2017 (the &#147;Credit Agreement&#148;). The Fourth Amendment provided for a new Term B Loan facility in the principal
amount of $542.3&nbsp;million, the proceeds of which (along with cash on hand) were used to repay in full the existing Term B Loan facility. Under the terms of the Fourth Amendment, the maturity date of the new Term B Loan facility remains
April&nbsp;26, 2024, but the new Term B Loan facility has an interest rate of LIBOR (as defined in the Credit Agreement) plus a percentage ranging from 2.00% to 2.25% for Eurocurrency Loans (as defined in the Credit Agreement) or the prime rate (as
determined in accordance with the Credit Agreement) plus a percentage ranging from 1.00% to 1.25% for Base Rate Loans (as defined in the Credit Agreement), in either case depending on ARRIS&#146;s Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio. The Fourth
Amendment also increased to $500&nbsp;million the amount of cash that can be used to offset indebtedness in the calculation of the Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio for purposes of determining the applicable interest rate. All other material terms of
the Credit Agreement remained unchanged. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On October&nbsp;17, 2017, we entered into the Third Amendment and Consent (the
&#147;Third Amendment&#148;) to the Credit Agreement. Pursuant to the Third Amendment, ARRIS (i)&nbsp;incurred &#147;Refinancing Term A Loans&#148; of $391&nbsp;million, (ii)&nbsp;incurred &#147;Refinancing Term
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1</FONT> Loans&#148; of $1,250&nbsp;million, and (iii)&nbsp;obtained a &#147;Refinancing Revolving Credit Facility&#148; of $500&nbsp;million, the proceeds of which were used to refinance in full the existing Term
A Loans, the existing Term <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1</FONT> Loans and the existing Revolving Credit Loans outstanding under the Credit Agreement immediately prior to the effectiveness of the Third Amendment. The existing Term B Loans were
not refinanced and remain outstanding. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Third Amendment extended the maturity date of the Term A Loans and the Revolving
Credit Facility to October&nbsp;17, 2022. Pursuant to the Third Amendment, ARRIS is subject to a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio test, which is unchanged from the Credit Agreement. In addition, the Company is subject to a maximum
consolidated net leverage ratio test of not more than 4.0:1.0, subject to a step-down to 3.75:1.00 commencing with the fiscal quarter ending March&nbsp;31, 2019. The amount of unrestricted cash used to offset indebtedness in the calculation of the
consolidated net leverage ratio was also increased from $200&nbsp;million to $500&nbsp;million. The interest rates under the Third Amendment were not changed. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On April&nbsp;26, 2017, we entered into a Second Amendment (the &#147;Second Amendment&#148;) to the Credit Agreement. The Second Amendment provided for a new Term B Loan facility in the principal amount
of $545&nbsp;million, the proceeds of which (along with cash on hand) were used to repay the existing Term B Loan facility. Under the terms of the Second Amendment, the new Term <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">B-2</FONT> Loan has a maturity date of
April 2024 and an interest rate of LIBOR plus a percentage ranging from 2.25% to 2.50% for Eurocurrency Rate Loans (as defined in the Credit Agreement), or the prime rate plus a percentage ranging from 1.25% to 1.50% for Base Rate Loans (as defined
in the Amended Credit Agreement), in either case depending on the Company&#146;s consolidated net leverage ratio. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Interest
rates on borrowings under the senior secured credit facilities are set forth in the table below. As of December&nbsp;31, 2017, we had $386.1&nbsp;million, $1,234.4&nbsp;million and $540.9&nbsp;million principal amounts outstanding under the Term
Loan A, Term Loan <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1</FONT> and Term Loan <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">B-3</FONT> Facilities. No borrowings existed under the Revolving Credit Facility and there were letters of credit totaling $1.7&nbsp;million
issued under the Revolving Credit Facility. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Credit Agreement provides for certain adjustments to the interest rates paid on the Term
Loan A, Term Loan <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1,</FONT> Term Loan <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">B-3</FONT> and Revolving Credit Facility based upon the achievement of certain leverage ratios. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Borrowings under the senior secured credit facilities are secured by first priority liens on substantially all of the assets of ARRIS and
certain of its present and future subsidiaries who are or become parties to, or guarantors under, the Credit Agreement governing the senior secured credit facilities. The Credit Agreement provides terms for mandatory prepayments and optional
prepayments and commitment reductions. The Credit Agreement also includes events of default, which are customary for facilities of this type (with customary grace periods, as applicable), including provisions under which, upon the occurrence of an
event of default, all amounts outstanding under the credit facilities may be accelerated. The Credit Agreement contains usual and customary limitations on indebtedness, liens, restricted payments, acquisitions and asset sales in the form of
affirmative, negative and financial covenants, which are customary for financings of this type, including the maintenance of a minimum interest coverage ratio and a maximum leverage ratio. As of December&nbsp;31, 2017, ARRIS was in compliance with
all covenants under the Credit Agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In connection with the Pace combination, ARRIS assumed an
accounts receivable financing program which was entered into by Pace on June&nbsp;30, 2015. Under this program, ARRIS assigned trade receivables on a revolving basis of up to $50&nbsp;million to the lender and the lender advanced 95% of the
receivable value to us. The remaining 5% was remitted to ARRIS upon receipt of cash from the customer. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The accounts receivable
financing program is accounted for as secured borrowings and amounts outstanding are included in the current portion of long-term debt on the consolidated balance sheet. We pay certain transaction fees and interest of 1.23% on the outstanding
balance in connection with this program. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As of December&nbsp;31, 2016, we had no outstanding balance under this program and
the program was terminated as of June&nbsp;30, 2017. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Commitments </I></FONT></P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>2017 vs. 2016 </U> </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Consolidated net income including adjustments, as per the table above, increased $183.2&nbsp;million during 2017 as compared to 2016. It should be noted that net income in 2017 includes 1)
$61.5&nbsp;million of expense related to the cash settlement of stock-based awards held by transferring employees in our Ruckus acquisition and 2) restructuring costs of $20.9&nbsp;million, and 3) inventory
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">step-up</FONT> in fair market value of $8.5&nbsp;million. The net income reflected in 2016 includes: 1) restructuring costs of $96.3&nbsp;million, 2) withholding tax of $54.7&nbsp;million and 3) inventory <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">step-up</FONT> in fair market value of $51.4&nbsp;million. These 2016 items were either not present or less significant in 2017. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Accounts receivable decreased $175.9&nbsp;million in 2017. This increase was primarily a result of purchasing pattern and payment patterns of our customers. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Inventory increased by $224.6&nbsp;million in 2017, reflecting timing of customer requirements and anticipated demand for certain
products, inventory acquired in the Ruckus acquisition, and the transition of component inventory from outsourced assemblers to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-house</FONT> production. In 2017 and 2016, we recognized reductions of
$8.5&nbsp;million and $51.4&nbsp;million, respectively, related to turnaround effects of inventory markups in acquisition accounting. We anticipate reducing inventory in 2018. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">67 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Accounts payable and accrued liabilities increased by $50.0&nbsp;million in 2017. The change
reflects an increase in accounts payable due to timing of payments primarily for inventory and was partially offset by reduction in accrued expenses and deferred revenues. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">All other accounts, net, include the changes in other receivables, income taxes payable (recoverable), and prepaids. The other receivables represent amounts due from our contract manufacturers for
material used in the assembly of our finished goods. The change in our income taxes recoverable account is a result of the timing of the actual estimated tax payments during the year as compared to the actual tax liability for the year. The net
change during 2017 was approximately $101.2&nbsp;million as compared to $66.1&nbsp;million in 2016. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I><U>2016 vs. 2015 </U>
</I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Consolidated net (loss) income including adjustments, decreased $29.6&nbsp;million during 2016 as compared to 2015. The
net loss reflected in the 2016 includes: 1) restructuring costs of $96.3&nbsp;million, 2) acquisition and integration costs of $53.2&nbsp;million, 3) withholding tax of $54.7&nbsp;million and 4) inventory
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">step-up</FONT> in fair market value of $51.4&nbsp;million. These items were either not present or were insignificant in 2015. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Accounts receivable increased by $258.7&nbsp;million during 2016. The increase was primarily a result of normal purchasing pattern and payment patterns of our customers. A significant component of this
change was an increase in accounts receivable due to the acquisition of Pace. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Inventory decreased by $282.6&nbsp;million
during 2016, reflecting the timing of customer requirements and anticipated demand for certain products. In 2016, there was a $51.4&nbsp;million reduction related to turnaround effect of inventory markup in acquisition accounting. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Accounts payable and accrued liabilities decreased by $178.1&nbsp;million during 2016, reflecting timing of payments. The Company acquired
$799.8&nbsp;million of accounts payable and accrued liabilities as part of the Pace combination. We acquired $298.7&nbsp;million of cash as part of the Pace combination. This cash is netted against the cash used for acquisitions in the investing
section of the cash flow statement and is not included in the operating section. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">All other accounts, net, include changes in
other receivables, income taxes payable (recoverable), and prepaid expenses. The other receivables represent amounts due from our contract manufacturers for material used in the assembly of our finished goods. The change in our income taxes
recoverable account is a result of the timing of the actual estimated tax payments during the year as compared to the actual tax liability for the year. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Proceeds from issuance of shares, net</I> &#151; Represents cash proceeds related to the vesting of
restricted share units, offset with expenses paid related to the issuance of shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Repurchase of shares</I> &#151;
Represents the cash used to buy back the Company&#146;s ordinary shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Excess tax benefits from stock-based compensation
plans </I>&#151; Represents the cash that otherwise would have been paid for income taxes if increases in the value of equity instruments also had not been deductible in determining taxable income. Prospectively, all excess tax benefits from
share-based payments will be reported as operating activities under new guidance, see Note 3 <I>Impact of Recently Issued Accounting Standards</I> of Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for disclosures related to the impact of recently
adopted accounting standards. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Repurchase of shares to satisfy employee minimum tax withholdings</I> &#151; Represents the
shares withheld and cancelled for cash, to satisfy the employee minimum tax withholding when restricted stock units vest. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Proceeds from issuance of debt</I> &#151; Represents the proceeds from new borrowings for our Term Loan Facilities upon the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">re-financing</FONT> of our Credit Agreement in 2017, and &#147;Term Loan <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1</FONT> Facility&#148; of $800&nbsp;million, which was funded upon the closing of the Pace combination in 2016.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Payment of debt obligation</I> &#151; Represents the mandatory payment of the term loans under the senior secured credit
facilities, payments to lenders exiting our credit facilities upon <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">re-financing,</FONT> as well as the repayment of debt assumed and settled in conjunction with the closing of the Pace combination in 2016 and
ActiveVideo acquisition in 2015. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Payment of financing lease obligation</I> &#151; Represents the amortization related to
the portion of the sale of building that did not qualify for sale-leaseback accounting. </FONT></P>
