</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Senior Secured Credit Facilities </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On December&nbsp;20, 2017, the Company entered into a Fourth Amendment (the &#147;Fourth Amendment&#148;) to its Amended and Restated
Credit Facility dated June&nbsp;18, 2015, as previously amended on December&nbsp;14, 2015, April&nbsp;26, 2017, and October&nbsp;17, 2017 (the &#147;Credit Agreement&#148;). The Fourth Amendment provided for a new Term B Loan facility in the
principal amount of $542.3&nbsp;million, the proceeds of which (along with cash on hand) were used to repay in full the existing Term B Loan facility. Under the terms of the Fourth Amendment, the maturity date of the new Term B Loan facility remains
April&nbsp;26, 2024, but the new Term B Loan facility has an interest rate of LIBOR (as defined in the Credit Agreement) plus a percentage ranging from 2.00% to 2.25% for Eurocurrency Loans (as defined in the Credit Agreement) or the prime rate (as
determined in accordance with the Credit Agreement) plus a percentage ranging from 1.00% to 1.25% for Base Rate Loans (as defined in the Credit Agreement), in either case depending on ARRIS&#146;s consolidated net leverage ratio. The Fourth
Amendment also increased to $500&nbsp;million the amount of cash that can be used to offset indebtedness in the calculation of the consolidated net leverage ratio for purposes of determining the applicable interest rate. All other material terms of
the Credit Agreement remained unchanged. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On October&nbsp;17, 2017, the Company entered into the Third Amendment and Consent
(the &#147;Third Amendment&#148;) to the Credit Agreement. Pursuant to the Third Amendment, ARRIS (i)&nbsp;incurred &#147;Refinancing Term A Loans&#148; of $391&nbsp;million, (ii)&nbsp;incurred &#147;Refinancing Term
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1</FONT> Loans&#148; of $1,250&nbsp;million, and (iii)&nbsp;obtained a &#147;Refinancing Revolving Credit Facility&#148; of $500&nbsp;million, the proceeds of which were used to refinance in full the existing Term
A Loans, the existing Term <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">A-1</FONT> Loans and the existing Revolving Credit Loans outstanding under the Credit Agreement immediately prior to the effectiveness of the Third Amendment. The existing Term B Loans were
not refinanced and remain outstanding. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">127
</FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Third Amendment extended the maturity date of the Term A Loans and the Revolving Credit
Facility to October&nbsp;17, 2022. Pursuant to the Third Amendment, the Company is subject to a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio test, which is unchanged from the Credit Agreement. In addition, the Company is subject to a maximum
consolidated net leverage ratio test of not more than 4.0:1.0, subject to a step-down to 3.75:1.00 commencing with the fiscal quarter ending March&nbsp;31, 2019. The amount of unrestricted cash used to offset indebtedness in the calculation of the
consolidated net leverage ratio was also increased from $200&nbsp;million to $500&nbsp;million. The interest rates under the Third Amendment were not changed. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On April&nbsp;26, 2017, ARRIS entered into a Second Amendment (the &#147;Second Amendment&#148;) to the Credit Agreement. The Second Amendment provided for a new Term B Loan facility in the principal
amount of $545&nbsp;million, the proceeds of which (along with cash on hand) were used to repay the existing Term B Loan facility. Under the terms of the Second Amendment, the new Term <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">B-2</FONT> Loan has a maturity
date of April 2024 and an interest rate of LIBOR plus a percentage ranging from 2.25% to 2.50% for Eurocurrency Rate Loans (as defined in the Credit Agreement), or the prime rate plus a percentage ranging from 1.25% to 1.50% for Base Rate Loans (as
defined in the Credit Agreement), in either case depending on the Company&#146;s consolidated net leverage ratio. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In
connection with the Amendments in 2017, the Company paid and capitalized approximately $1.4&nbsp;million of financing fees and $4.5&nbsp;million of original issuance discount. In addition, the Company expensed approximately $4.5&nbsp;million of debt
issuance costs and wrote off approximately $1.3&nbsp;million of existing debt issuance costs associated with certain lenders who were not party to the credit facility, which were included as interest expense in the Consolidated Statements of Income
for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Interest rates on borrowings under the senior secured credit facilities are set

certain of its present and future subsidiaries who are or become parties to, or guarantors under, the Credit Agreement governing the senior secured credit facilities. The Credit Agreement provides terms for mandatory prepayments and optional
prepayments and commitment reductions. The Credit Agreement also includes events of default, which are customary for facilities of this type (with customary grace periods, as applicable), including provisions under which, upon the occurrence of an
event of default, all amounts outstanding under the credit facilities may be accelerated. The Credit Agreement contains usual and customary limitations on indebtedness, liens, restricted payments, acquisitions and asset sales in the form of
affirmative, negative and financial covenants, which are customary for financings of this type, including the maintenance of a minimum interest coverage ratio and a maximum leverage ratio. As of December&nbsp;31, 2017, ARRIS was in compliance with
all covenants under the Credit Agreement. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2017, the Company made mandatory payments of approximately $91.7&nbsp;million

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Account Receivable Financing Program </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In connection with the Pace combination on January&nbsp;4, 2016, ARRIS assumed an accounts receivable financing program which was entered
into by Pace on June&nbsp;30, 2015. Under this program, the Company assigned trade receivables on a revolving basis of up to $50&nbsp;million to the lender and the lender advances 95% of the receivable value to the Company. The remaining 5% is
remitted to ARRIS upon receipt of cash from the customer. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The accounts receivable financing program was accounted for as
secured borrowings and amounts outstanding were included in the current portion of long-term debt on the consolidated balance sheet. The Company paid certain transaction fees and interest of 1.23% on the outstanding balance in connection with this
program. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As of December&nbsp;31, 2016, there is no outstanding balance under this program and the program was terminated as of
June&nbsp;30, 2017. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Other </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, the Company issued 2.6&nbsp;million
shares of its ordinary shares related to the vesting of restricted stock units, as compared to 2.3&nbsp;million shares for the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2016. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The warrants have a dilutive effect in those periods in which the average market price of the shares exceeds the current effective exercise price (under the treasury stock method), and are not subject to
performance conditions. During the fourth quarter of 2016, approximately 2.2&nbsp;million warrants vested based on the amount of purchases of products and services by the customer from the Company. There was no vesting in 2017. The dilutive effect
of these vested shares was immaterial. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In connection with the Pace combination in 2016, ARRIS issued approximately
47.7&nbsp;million ordinary shares as part of the purchase consideration. The fair value of the 47.7&nbsp;million shares issued, $1,434.7&nbsp;million, was determined based on the conversion of each of Pace&#146;s shares and equity awards outstanding
at a conversion rate of 0.1455 with a value of $30.08 at January&nbsp;4, 2016, which represents the opening price of the Company&#146;s shares at the date of Pace combination. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company has not paid cash dividends on its stock since its inception. Any future determination to pay dividends will be at the discretion of the Board of Directors and will be dependent on
then-existing conditions, including the Company&#146;s financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, contractual and legal restrictions, business prospects and other factors that the Board considers relevant. The Credit Agreement
contains restrictions on the Company&#146;s ability to pay dividends on its ordinary shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Note 17. Warrants </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2016, the Company entered into two separate Warrant and Registration Rights Agreements (the &#147;Warrants&#148;) with certain
customers pursuant to which those customers may purchase up to 14.0&nbsp;million of ARRIS&#146;s ordinary shares, (subject to adjustment in accordance with the terms of the Warrants, the &#147;Shares&#148;). </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Warrants will vest in tranches based on the amount of purchases of products and services by the customer from the Company. At
December&nbsp;31, 2017, approximately 2.2&nbsp;million Warrants were vested and outstanding, with a weighted average exercise price of $24.56, which vested based on the amount of purchases of products and services by the customers from the Company
in 2016. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The ordinary shares issuable under our outstanding Warrant program with a customer, based on achieving certain
purchase levels in 2018, are between 1.0&nbsp;million and 2.5&nbsp;million at an exercise price for the warrants of $26.14. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For Warrants, other than those issuable in 2018, the exercise price per Share was established based upon the average volume-weighted price
of ARRIS&#146;s ordinary shares on NASDAQ for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10-day</FONT> trading period preceding the date of the Warrants. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For Warrants issuable in 2018, the exercise price was set based on the volume-weighted price for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10-day</FONT> trading period preceding January&nbsp;1, 2018.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Warrants provide for net Share settlement that, if elected by the holders, will reduce the number of Shares issued upon
exercise to reflect net settlement of the exercise price. Customers&#146; may also request cash settlement of the Warrants upon exercise in lieu of issuing Shares, however, such cash election is at the discretion of ARRIS. The Warrants will expire
by September&nbsp;30, 2023. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Warrants provide for certain adjustments that may be made to the exercise price and the number
of Shares issuable upon exercise due to customary anti-dilution provisions based on future corporate events. In addition, in connection with any consolidation, merger or similar extraordinary event involving the Company, the Warrants will be deemed
to represent the right to receive, upon exercise, the same consideration received by the holders of the Company&#146;s ordinary shares in connection with such transaction. Upon a change of control of ARRIS or if ARRIS materially breaches its
applicable agreements with customers (and such breach is not cured pursuant to the terms of the agreements), the Warrants will immediately vest for the minimum threshold of Shares that would otherwise be issuable. </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ARRIS has also agreed, if requested by the holders, to register the Shares issuable upon
exercise of the Warrants under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &#147;Securities Act&#148;) and has also granted &#147;piggyback&#148; registration rights in the event ARRIS files a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and
Exchange Commission under the Securities Act covering its equity securities, subject to the terms and conditions included in the Warrants. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Because the Warrants contain performance criteria, which includes aggregate purchase levels and product mix, under which customers must achieve for the Warrants to vest, as detailed above, the final
measurement date for the Warrants is the date on which the Warrants vest. Prior to the final measurement, when achievement of the performance criteria has been deemed probable, the estimated fair value of Warrants is being recorded as a reduction to
net sales based on the projected number of Warrants expected to vest, the proportion of purchases by customers and its affiliates within the period relative to the aggregate purchase levels required for the Warrants to vest and the then-current fair
value of the related Warrants. To the extent that projections change in the future as to the number of Warrants that will vest, as well as changes in the fair market value of the Warrants, a cumulative
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">catch-up</FONT> adjustment will be recorded in the period in which the estimates change. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The
fair value of the Warrants is determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model. The assumptions utilized in the Black-Scholes model include the risk-free interest rate, expected volatility, and expected life in years. The risk-free interest
rate over the expected life is equal to the prevailing U.S. Treasury note rate over the same period. Expected volatility is determined utilizing historical volatility over a period of time equal to the expected life of the warrant. Expected life is
equal to the remaining contractual term of the warrant. The dividend yield is assumed to be zero since we have not historically declared dividends and do not have any plans to declare dividends in the future. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017 and 2016, ARRIS recorded zero and $30.2&nbsp;million, respectively, as a reduction to net sales
in connection with Warrants. This transaction is considered an equity contract, and is classified as such. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Note 18. Income Taxes

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On December&nbsp;22, 2017, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (the &#147;Act&#148;) was signed into law
making significant changes to the Internal Revenue Code. Changes include, but are not limited to, a corporate tax rate decrease from 35% to 21% effective for tax years beginning after December&nbsp;31, 2017, a
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> transition tax </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">132
</FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">
on the mandatory deemed repatriation of cumulative foreign earnings as of December&nbsp;31, 2017, a new alternative U.S. tax on certain Base Erosion Anti-Avoidance (BEAT) payments from a U.S.
company to any foreign related party, a new U.S. tax on certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">off-shore</FONT> earnings referred to as Global Intangible <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Low-Taxed</FONT> Income (GILTI), additional limitations on
certain executive compensation, and limitations on interest deductions. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company was required to recognize the effect of
the tax law changes in the period of enactment, such as determining the transition tax, remeasuring its U.S. deferred tax assets and liabilities as well as reassessing the realizability of its deferred tax assets. The Company has calculated its best
estimate of the impact of the Act in its year end income tax provision in accordance with its understanding of the Act and guidance available as of the date of this filing and as a result has recorded ($22.5) million as an income tax benefit in the
fourth quarter of 2017, the period in which the legislation was enacted. The provisional amount related to the remeasurement of certain deferred tax assets and liabilities based on the rates at which they are expected to reverse in the future was
($22.3) million. The provisional amount related to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> transition tax on the mandatory deemed repatriation of foreign earnings was ($0.2) million based on cumulative foreign earnings of
$32.4&nbsp;million. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On December&nbsp;22, 2017, Staff Accounting Bulletin No.&nbsp;118 (&#147;SAB 118&#148;) was issued to
address the application of U.S. GAAP in situations when a registrant does not have the necessary information available, prepared, or analyzed (including computations) in reasonable detail to complete the accounting for certain income tax effects of
the Act. SAB 118 allows us to record these provisional amounts during a measurement period not to extend beyond one year of the enactment date. In accordance with SAB 118, the Company has determined that the ($22.3) million of the deferred tax
benefit recorded in connection with the remeasurement of certain deferred tax assets and liabilities and the ($0.2) million of current tax benefit recorded in connection with the transition tax on the mandatory deemed repatriation of foreign
earnings was a provisional amount and a reasonable estimate at December&nbsp;31, 2017. Since the Act was passed late in the fourth quarter of 2017, and ongoing guidance and accounting interpretation are expected over the next 12 months, we consider
the accounting for the transition tax, deferred tax <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">re-measurements,</FONT> and other items to be incomplete due to additional work necessary to (1)&nbsp;do a more detailed analysis of historical foreign earnings as
well as potential correlative adjustments; (2)&nbsp;determine <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">re-measurement</FONT> of any changes to deferred tax assets and liabilities associated with any acquisition accounting adjustments for fair value
adjustments made within the acquisition accounting measurement period; (3)&nbsp;assess any forthcoming guidance; and (4)&nbsp;finalize our ongoing analysis of final <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-end</FONT> data and tax positions. Any
subsequent adjustment to these amounts will be recorded to tax expense in the quarter of 2018 when the analysis is complete. We expect to complete our analysis within the measurement period in accordance with SAB 118. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ARRIS&#146; ability to use U.S. federal, state, and other foreign net operating loss carryforwards to reduce future taxable income, or to
use U.S. federal and state research and development tax credit and other carryforwards to reduce future income tax liabilities, is subject to the ability to generate sufficient taxable income of an appropriate characterization in the appropriate
taxing jurisdictions. In some instance the utilization is also subject to restrictions attributable to change of ownership during prior tax years. as defined by appropriate law in the relevant taxing jurisdiction. These limitations, as noted above,
prevent the Company from utilizing certain deferred tax assets and were considered in establishing our valuation allowances. </FONT></P>

<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.K.</FONT> earnings is not practicable because of the complexities associated with this hypothetical calculation. Furthermore, the Company does not assert indefinite reinvestment on its earnings of foreign
subsidiaries that are not directly or indirectly owned by a U.S. shareholder, and have recorded a deferred tax liability of $2.7 million associated with the unremitted earnings of those subsidiaries. </FONT></P>

state and other foreign jurisdictions. As of December&nbsp;31, 2017, the Company and its subsidiaries were under income tax audit in various jurisdictions including the United Kingdom, the United States, Hong Kong and various states and other
foreign countries. ARRIS does not anticipate audit adjustments in excess of its current accrual for uncertain tax positions. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Liabilities related to uncertain tax positions inclusive of interest and penalties were $178.2&nbsp;million and $137.2&nbsp;million at
December&nbsp;31, 2017 and 2016, respectively. These liabilities at December&nbsp;31, 2017 and 2016 were reduced by $29.6&nbsp;million and $28.4&nbsp;million, respectively, for offsetting benefits from the corresponding effects of potential transfer
pricing adjustments, state income taxes and other unrecognized tax benefits. These offsetting benefits are recorded in other <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-current</FONT> assets and noncurrent deferred income taxes. The net result of
$148.6&nbsp;million and $108.7&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2017 and 2016, respectively, if recognized and released, would favorably affect tax expense. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Included in the net result of $148.6 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2017, is $37.9&nbsp;million of net acquired uncertain tax positions. This amount is fully indemnified and offset by a corresponding
indemnification asset recorded in other <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-current</FONT> assets. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company reported
approximately $4.0&nbsp;million and $9.2&nbsp;million, respectively, of interest and penalty accrual related to the anticipated payment of these potential tax liabilities as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and 2016. The Company classifies interest and
penalties recognized on the liability for uncertain tax positions as income tax expense. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Based on information currently
available, the Company anticipates that over the next twelve-month period, statutes of limitations may close and audit settlements will occur relating to existing unrecognized tax benefits of approximately $15.6&nbsp;million primarily arising from
U.S. federal and state tax related items. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Note 19. Stock-Based Compensation </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ARRIS grants stock awards under its 2016 Stock Incentive Plan (&#147;SIP&#148;). Upon approval of the 2016 SIP, all shares available for
grant under the Company&#146;s other existing stock incentive plans were no longer available. The Board of Directors approved the SIP and the prior plans to facilitate the retention and continued motivation of key employees, consultants and
directors, and to align more closely their interests with those of the Company and its stockholders. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Awards under the SIP may
be in the form of stock options, stock grants, stock units, restricted stock, stock appreciation rights, performance shares and units, and dividend equivalent rights. A total of 31,215,000 shares of

requisite services period for the restricted shares. The Company applies an estimated forfeiture rate based upon historical rates. The fair value is the market price of the underlying ordinary shares on the date of grant. </FONT></P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Restricted Shares Units &#151; Subject to Comparative Market Performance</U> </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ARRIS grants to certain employees restricted shares units, in which the number of shares to be issued is dependent upon the Company&#146;s
total shareholder return as compared to the shareholder return of the NASDAQ composite over a three-year period. The number of shares which could potentially be issued ranges from zero to 200% of the target award. For the awards granted in 2015, the
three-year measurement period ended on December&nbsp;31, 2017. The Company&#146;s total shareholder return underperformed the NASDAQ composite over the three-year period, therefore resulted in zero achievement of the target award. The remaining
grants outstanding that are subject to market performance are 672,530 shares at target; at 200% performance 1,345,060 would be issued. Compensation expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the three-year measurement period and is based
upon the fair market value of the shares expected to vest. The fair value of the restricted share units is estimated on the date of grant using a Monte Carlo Simulation model. </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The total fair value of restricted share units, including both <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-performance</FONT> and performance-related shares, that vested during 2017, 2016 and 2015 was $76.1&nbsp;million, $52.3&nbsp;million and $118.3&nbsp;million, respectively. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Employee Stock Purchase Plan (&#147;ESPP&#148;)</U> </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ARRIS offers an ESPP to certain employees. The plan complies with Section&nbsp;423 of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code, which provides that employees will not be immediately taxed on the difference between
the market price of the stock and a discounted purchase price if it meets certain requirements. Participants can request that up to 10% of their base compensation be applied toward the purchase of ARRIS ordinary shares under ARRIS&#146;s ESPP.
Purchases by any one participant are limited to $25,000 (based upon the fair market value) in any one year. The exercise price is the lower of 85% of the fair market value of the ARRIS ordinary shares on either the first day of the purchase period
or the last day of the purchase period. A plan provision which allows for the more favorable of two exercise prices is commonly referred to as a &#147;look-back&#148; feature. Any discount offered in excess of five percent generally will be
considered compensatory and appropriately is recognized as compensation expense. Additionally, any ESPP offering a look-back feature is considered compensatory. ARRIS uses the Black-Scholes option valuation model to value shares issued under the
ESPP. The valuation is comprised of two components; the 15% discount of a share of ordinary shares and 85% of a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> option held (related to the look-back feature). The weighted average assumptions used
to estimate the fair value of purchase rights granted under the ESPP for 2017, 2016 and 2015, were as follows: risk-free interest rates of 1.2%, 0.5% and 0.1%, respectively; a dividend yield of 0%; volatility factor of the expected market price of
ARRIS&#146;s stock of 0.28, 0.37, and 0.41, respectively; and a weighted average expected life of 0.5 year for each. The Company recorded stock compensation expense related to the ESPP of approximately $4.8&nbsp;million, $4.6&nbsp;million and
$5.1&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><U>Unrecognized Compensation
Cost</U> </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As of December&nbsp;31, 2017, there was approximately $152.2&nbsp;million of total unrecognized compensation cost
related to unvested share-based awards granted under the Company&#146;s incentive plans. This compensation cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.8 years. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Note 20. Employee Benefit Plans </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company sponsors a qualified and a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-qualified</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-contributory</FONT> defined benefit pension plan that covers certain U.S. and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> employees. As of January&nbsp;1,
2000, the Company froze the U.S. qualified defined pension plan benefits for its participants. These participants elected to enroll in ARRIS&#146;s enhanced 401(k) plan. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The U.S. pension plan benefit formulas generally provide for payments to retired employees based upon their length of service and compensation as defined in the plans. ARRIS&#146;s investment policy is to
fund the qualified plan as required by the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (&#147;ERISA&#148;) and to the extent that such contributions are tax deductible. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ARRIS also provides a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-contributory</FONT> defined benefit plan which cover employees in Taiwan. Any other benefit plans outside of the U.S. are not material to ARRIS
either individually or in the aggregate. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">No minimum funding contributions are required in 2017 under the Company&#146;s U.S.
defined benefit plan. For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, the Company made a voluntary minimum funding contribution of $1.4&nbsp;million to its U.S defined benefit plan.&nbsp;The Company also made funding contributions of $1.2&nbsp;million
related to our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> pension plan in 2017. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2016, in an effort to reduce
future premiums and administrative fees as well as to increase our funded status in connection with our U.S. pension obligation, we made a voluntary funding contribution of $5.0&nbsp;million. The Company also made funding contributions of
$10.9&nbsp;million related to our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> pension plan in 2016. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company has
established a rabbi trust to fund the pension obligations of the Executive Chairman under his Supplemental Retirement Plan including the benefit under the Company&#146;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-qualified</FONT> defined benefit plan.

invest conservatively so as not to expose assets to depreciation in adverse markets. The plans&#146; strategy also places a high priority on earning a rate of return greater than the annual inflation rate along with maintaining average market
results. The plan has targeted asset diversification across different asset classes and markets to take advantage of economic environments and to also act as a risk minimizer by dampening the portfolio&#146;s volatility. The following table

terminated earlier by a Board resolution, this new plan will expire when ARRIS has used all authorized funds for repurchase. However, U.K. law also generally prohibits a company from repurchasing its own shares through &#147;off market
purchases&#148; without prior approval of shareholders because we are not traded on a recognized investment exchange in the U.K. This shareholder approval lasts for a maximum period of five years. Prior to and in connection with the Pace
combination, we obtained approval to purchase our own shares. This authority to repurchase shares terminates in January 2021, unless otherwise reapproved by our shareholders. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
